subject: Chile
note: Cited to pinned Wikipedia revisions (trusted_secondary): Valparaíso, Aconcagua, National Route 7 (Argentina). The profile is computed from NOAA ETOPO 2022 (1 arc-minute grid, about 1.8 km cells, public domain) along a straight great-circle line through four stops; 895.5 km, lowest -87 m at the start, highest 4,849 m at 185.9 km. The grid smooths peaks, so this is the model's height along the line, not a surveyed section and not the road (the road winds). The panel prints the vertical stretch.

claims.text: Valparaíso is a major seaport of Chile and one of the Pacific Ocean's most important seaports.
A straight cut of 895 km from Valparaíso to the plain in Argentina (computed from NOAA ETOPO 2022, not the road).
Along that cut the model's height rises from -87 m at the coast to 4,849 m at 186 km (computed from NOAA ETOPO 2022; 1.8 km cells smooth the peaks).
Aconcagua, in Mendoza Province, Argentina, has a summit elevation of 6,967.15 metres and is the highest mountain outside Asia; it lies about 15 kilometres from the Argentine–Chilean border.
The old road to the Chilean border is a zigzagging road from Las Cuevas to La Cumbre Pass, where the statue Christ the Redeemer of the Andes stands.
